newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end lower on speculative selling.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end lower on speculative selling.

text.p: Brazilian shares ended slightly lower on speculative selling late in the session amid a new corruption scandal in Congress, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 48 most traded stocks closed off 0.32 percent at 10,647 points. Volume totalled 761.5 million reais ($718.3 million).
Local shares opened lower as a press report that deputies allegedly received money to vote for a constitutional amendment allowing presidential re-election prompted a widely expected profit-taking.

The market bounced back and traded higher until news broke that a lower house panel which was due to vote on a bill outlining the rules for the privatization of Brazil's telecommunications sector Tuesday decided to put off the voting.

Telecommunications stocks, which had been climbing on optimism over legislative progress in the General Telecommunications Law and higher premiums on the Band B cellular selloff, fell after the news, traders said.
Telebras preferred dropped 1.1 percent to close at 135.20 reais, while its common stock lost 0.4 percent, ending at 127.99 reais.
Other telecom shares, however, managed to end higher. Telesp rose 0.3 percent.

Analysts said stock prices could rebound Wednesday, but some said trend for the bolsa would also depend on how the government handles the corruption scandal in order to guarantee progress of the re-election bill and key constitutional reforms in Congress.
Among other blue-chips, CVRD preferred continued to lose ground post-privatization and fell 3.2 percent to end at 24.20 reais.

Federal power utility Eletrobras gained 2.16 percent, ending at 521 reais. It contributed to a 1.11 percent rise in the power sector index which comprises the nine most liquid shares of the electrical industry.
Stocks of CSN, the leader of the consortium that bought a controlling stake in CVRD, ended flat at 37.60 reais.
